title: Extending degreewise perfect open-site stalk maps
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open, $x\in U$, and $P,Q$ cochain complexes of module sheaves on the slice site over $U$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume only $P$ is strictly perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Write $T$ for the termwise open module stalk functor [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor]. Given arbitrary degreewise morphisms $t_n:T(P)^n\to T(Q)^n$, there are an affine open $W\subseteq U$ containing $x$, its restriction functor $R$, its termwise stalk functor $S$, a natural isomorphism $e:R\circ S\cong T$ in functor order, and component maps $g_n:R(P)^n\to R(Q)^n$ such that $S(g_n)=e_P^n\,t_n\,(e_Q^{-1})^n$ in categorical composition order. No differential compatibility of the input or output family is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Tags 09RE (affine finite-presentation calculation) and 01CP (internal-Hom stalk comparison); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09RE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01CP, read 2026-10-13

proof.text: Pass to the open subscheme U by the slice-site equivalence. Each term of P is a finite-free retract and hence finitely presented. The internal-Hom stalk comparison is an isomorphism for this source and arbitrary target Q.X n. Take the preimage of each prescribed stalk component and represent that internal-Hom germ by a local morphism.

Choose integer bounds a,b for P. Only n in [a,b] have nonzero source; for every other n use the zero map. Intersect the finitely many representing neighbourhoods for n in [a,b] with U and choose an affine neighbourhood W of x inside this intersection. Restrict each local morphism to W. The empty interval case uses zero maps in all degrees.

Neighbourhoods inside W are cofinal among neighbourhoods inside U. Together with the open immersion stalk-ring isomorphisms and the slice-site equivalences, this gives a natural isomorphism from restriction followed by the W stalk to the U stalk. Apply it termwise to complexes. Its germ formula and the canonical internal-Hom comparison formula show that the stalk of each chosen component is the prescribed component conjugated by this isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09RE and 01CP; V3 expands the finite-component argument to actual module stalks on the open slice site.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_perfect_open_stalk_degreewise_lift
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (P Q : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hP : IsStrictlyPerfect X U P)
    (t : ∀ n : ℤ,
      (((openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).X n ⟶
      (((openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q).X n) :
    ∃ (W : X.Opens) (hxW : x ∈ W) (_hW : IsAffineOpen W) (hWU : W ≤ U),
      let R := (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hWU : W ⟶ U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let S := (openModuleStalkFunctor X W ⟨x, hxW⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let T := (openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      ∃ (e : R ⋙ S ≅ T) (g : ∀ n : ℤ, (R.obj P).X n ⟶ (R.obj Q).X n),
        ∀ n : ℤ, (openModuleStalkFunctor X W ⟨x, hxW⟩).map (g n) =
          (e.app P).hom.f n ≫ t n ≫ (e.app Q).inv.f n
